newsitem.title: UK: N Sea Brent set to firm, Urals strong.
newsitem.headline: N Sea Brent set to firm, Urals strong.

text.p: North Sea Brent crude oil looked set to trade at firmer numbers again on Wednesday, though traders said the market was time-specific and the recent upward trend limited.
With only one or two Brent cargoes on offer and none coming through the chains on Wednesday, buyers were heard bidding at Tuesday's traded August +4 cents against one offer six cents higher.
"No-one thinks the market will hold with Iraq looming over our heads, but for the moment it is a sellers' market," one refiner said.
September Brent on the IPE traded up 15 cents at $18.74 a barrel, supported by bullish crude and gasoline figures from overnight U.S. weekly API statistics.
The API stock data showed an unexpectedly large draw of 9.7 million barrels on crude and a fall of 3.17 million barrels in gasoline stock levels.
No early CFD or Brent intermonth trades were reported although CFDs were well bid by two large trading houses, brokers said.
Next week's Aug 4-8 dates were bid at Sept evens with no offers and the Aug 11-15 bid at Sept -6 cents.

The only physical deal reported was an Ekofisk loading August 20 which traded at Dated Brent +28 cents, down from +34 cents at the end of last week. Most other sellers were heard holding out for last weeks levels, one trader said.
Brent intermonth talk firmed on the bid side with Aug/Sept buyers at +12 cents while the Sept/Oct was -2/0 and Oct/Nov -9/-6 cents, brokers said.
In the Mediterranean, the Urals market was still reaping the benefits of delays in the resumption of Iraqi exports, with second decade August cargoes fetching even stronger numbers than the first.
A 12-14 cargo was bought on Tuesday by a European major at Dated Brent -55 cents c+f Augusta, worth a few cents more on a cif basis.
This was firmer than a deal done on Monday for a 10-12 cargo at Dated Brent -62.5 cents cif Italy.
"It's a strong market from a sellers point of view, but buyers will not buy unless they have urgent requirements," said one trader.
Mediterranean traders are expecting Iraq to maintain the same price formula for the next round of sales as for the first 90 day period.
The formula links the price to Arab Light crude, and assuming differentials are unchanged, the August price of Kirkuk blend would be Dated Brent -$2.00 a barrel.
Nevertheless, some potential buyers of Iraqi crude said they were no longer expecting any Iraqi flows before the end of the current 90-day period, which lasts until September 5.
"We not expecting barrels before the end of August. I think they'll start from September 6," said one.
